text: I've cut wood for the kilns since I was twelve.
Bran is teaching me to judge a grove, not just cut it.
The cutting boundary keeps moving farther from the Citadel.
I went past the marked line into the Old Canal Bed once.
I found old brick foundations half-buried in dried silt, older than anything standing today.
I left quickly. Something about the place felt wrong, though nothing moved.
The woman in the abandoned house didn't seem surprised when I mentioned it.
Kiri and I trade stories at the pasture fence when our routes cross.
She says herders avoid a stretch of the old bed too.
That's twice now — a kiln-scout and a herder both avoiding the same ground independently.
Yara warned me once not to go past the marked stumps.
She wouldn't say why, only that it wasn't my business yet.
I was too young to remember when the river actually turned.
My mother says it happened over several dry years, not one night.
But some older folk in the Lower Town still tell it like it happened all at once.
I want to know which version is true.
Bran doesn't scold me for wandering. He just asks what I found.
I think he wanders too, in his own way, just slower and quieter about it.
I want to scout the far bed properly, not by accident.
